name: Static isotropic weak-field metric and Newtonian limit (Phi = G M/(c^2 r)); proper distance on the slice is int e^{-Phi} dl, and coordinate light time is int e^{-2Phi} dl

source.located: Textbook result, no single originating paper. The weak-field/post-Newtonian metric is READ in C.M. Will, 'The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment', arXiv:1403.7377v1 (Living Rev. Relativ. 17 (2014) 4): sec. 3.2 p.28 eq (30) U = int rho'|x-x'|^-1 d^3x'; p.29 ordering rules U ~ v^2 ~ Pi ~ p/rho ~ eps and 'A consistent post-Newtonian limit requires determination of g_00 correct through O(eps^2), g_0i through O(eps^3/2), and g_ij through O(eps)'; Table 2 p.29 (gamma = beta = 1 in GR); Box 2 p.30-31 (standard PPN gauge, G = c = 1, metric g_00 = -1 + 2U - 2 beta U^2 + ..., g_ij = (1 + 2 gamma U) delta_ij + O(eps^2)); sec. 4.1 pp.40-43 (deflection (1+gamma)/2 eq 59; round-trip delay 2(1+gamma)M ln(...) eq 62; Cassini gamma - 1 = (2.1 +- 2.3)e-5); Table 4 p.44; beta - 1 = (-4.1 +- 7.8)e-5 p.45. published_statement: Will 2014 (arXiv:1403.7377) p.28: 'in this limit, the spacetime metric g predicted by nearly every metric theory of gravity has the same structure. It can be written as an expansion about the Minkowski metric (eta_mu nu = diag(-1,1,1,1)) in terms of dimensionless gravitational potentials ... in imitation of the Newtonian gravitational potential U(x,t) = int rho(x',t)|x-x'|^-1 d^3x' (30).' p.29: 'The "order of smallness" is determined according to the rules U ~ v^2 ~ Pi ~ p/rho ~ eps ... (we use units in which G = c = 1) ... A consistent post-Newtonian limit requires determination of g_00 correct through O(eps^2), g_0i through O(eps^3/2), and g_ij through O(eps).' Box 2 p.31: 'g_00 = -1 + 2U - 2 beta U^2 - 2 xi Phi_W + ... + O(eps^3), ... g_ij = (1 + 2 gamma U) delta_ij + O(eps^2).' Table 2 p.29: gamma 'How much space-curvature produced by unit rest mass?' value in GR 1; beta 'How much nonlinearity in the superposition law for gravity?' value in GR 1. p.43: round-trip delay 'delta t = 2(1 + gamma) M_sun ln(...) (62)'; Cassini 2003 'gamma - 1 = (2.1 +- 2.3) x 10^-5'. TREE'S USE (phase1.py:70-81): 'For a static metric in isotropic form, g_tt = -e^{2Phi}, g_ij = e^{-2Phi} delta_ij, a payload at rest at A has four-velocity u = e^{-Phi} d/dt ... d(A,B) = int e^{-Phi} dl THE TRANSITION QUANTITY ... t(A,B) = int e^{-2Phi} dl THE PROPULSION QUANTITY. ONE Phi, TWO EXPONENTS, RATIO EXACTLY 2 (unified.py measured 1.9940 to 2.0229 over both signs of Phi).' SI conversion (phase1.py:364-366): 'Delta d = (G/c^2) M Lambda' as G_SI * M_kg / C_SI**2 * lam(b, a, Rs).
published_hypotheses: W1 (Will p.26) metric theory: symmetric metric, test bodies on geodesics, special-relativistic non-gravitational physics in local Lorentz frames (EEP)
W2 (Will p.28) slow-motion, weak-field limit: expansion about Minkowski in potentials of graded smallness
W3 (Will p.29) ordering U ~ v^2 ~ Pi ~ p/rho ~ eps -- in particular stresses/pressures small compared with rest-mass density, p/rho = O(eps)
W4 (Will p.29) the expansion is only fixed through O(eps^2) in g_00 and O(eps) in g_ij; the O(eps^2) term of g_ij is NOT determined by the post-Newtonian limit
W5 (Will Box 2 p.30) standard PPN gauge (isotropic g_ij at this order), G the Newtonian constant measured far from the system, U zero at infinity
W6 (Will Table 2) GR values gamma = beta = 1; experimental: gamma - 1 = (2.1 +- 2.3)e-5 (Cassini), beta - 1 = (-4.1 +- 7.8)e-5
W7 (Will eq 30) U is sourced by rest-mass density rho; the review's sources are positive-mass (solar system) bodies
hypothesis_drift: SIGN CONVENTION (implicit, not an error): with g_tt = -e^{2Phi} the Newtonian identification is Phi = -U = -GM/(c^2 r) (C3a/b). The canonical entry's name writes 'Phi = G M/(c^2 r)'. phase1 is internally consistent because its M is the MAGNITUDE of a NEGATIVE core mass: phi_device = +m/sqrt(r^2+a^2) - m/max(r,R_s) with m > 0 (phase1.py:261-263), 'everything above needs M < 0' (phase1.py:204), and contraction_law takes a positive M_kg (phase1.py:364-366). The negative-mass hypothesis is therefore carried by prose at phase1.py:204 and specthm.py:641 ('m < 0 locally'), not by the sign of contraction_law's argument. Recorded as a labelling discrepancy in the canonical name, not a refutation.

SINGLE-Phi EXPONENTIAL FORM (ADDED as an ansatz, which the canonical hypotheses already say): Will's W4 fixes g_ij only through O(eps). The tree's e^{-2Phi} fixes the O(Phi^2) term of g_ij at coefficient 2; exact Schwarzschild in isotropic coordinates (Ricci-flat, C3e) has 3/2 (C3d), while g_00 agrees through O(U^2) (beta = 1, C3c). For non-constant Phi the ansatz's Einstein tensor has G_ij purely quadratic in grad Phi and G_tt = e^{4Phi}(2 lap Phi - |grad Phi|^2) (C4b-d): it is an exact GR vacuum solution for no non-constant Phi, and it demands stresses of O(Phi^2). Inside W3 (p/rho = O(eps)) this is consistent; it is a definition of the tree's device metric, not a claim about GR's strong field (phase1.py:67-69).

'RATIO EXACTLY 2' (WORDING, already bounded by the canonical hypothesis): exact for the EXPONENTS by construction; for the SAVINGS the exact identity (1-e^{-2Phi}) = (1-e^{-Phi})(1+e^{-Phi}) makes the ratio 1 + e^{-Phi} = 2 - Phi + Phi^2/2 - ..., equal to 2 only at Phi = 0 (C2a-c). The owner prints both 'EXACTLY 2' and the measured 1.9940-2.0229 side by side (phase1.py:79-80), and the selftest carries rtol 5e-3 at m = 2e-2 (phase1.py:461); the measured values correspond to effective Phi = 6.0e-3 and -2.26e-2 (C2d/e). Consistent, first order. In PPN terms the ratio is (1+gamma)/gamma, so it also carries the hypothesis gamma = 1 (W6), which phase1 does not state.

WEAK FIELD DROPPED AT THE PRICE FIGURES (the one narrowing): contraction_law is the first-order (weak-field) law Delta d = m Lambda. phase1.py:180-181 and its selftest phase1.py:508-510, and index3.py:673, apply it to contract a 4 ly corridor by 1 % (2.57e10 M_sun) and by 50 % (1.28e12 M_sun). Lambda as used is the FULL-CROSSING integral (C6), so the endpoints lie outside the shell, R_s <= L/2; then the peak potential on the ray is Phi_max ~ m/b >= (Delta d/L) e^2/2 for ANY choice of R_s/b (C8a), and = 40.06 (Delta d/L) at the tree's R_s/b = 200. At 50 %: Phi_max >= 1.85 for any geometry, 19.93 at the tree's -- not weak field; the exact ansatz contraction int(1-e^{-Phi}) at the m the linear law demands is 80.6 b against the 200 b required (ratio 0.403, C8c). At 1 %: Phi_max = 0.399 at the tree's geometry, exact ansatz contraction 0.944 of the linear law (C8d) -- the weak-field law is ~6 % optimistic there, beyond the 1e-3 selftest tolerance printed on the figure. What GR (rather than the ansatz) gives at Phi ~ 20 is not computed here and is OPEN.

gamma = 1 FOR A NEGATIVE-MASS SOURCE (hypothesis carried, not stated): Will's data (W7) are all positive-mass solar-system sources. In GR the linearised field equations are linear in T, so gamma = 1 is predicted for either sign; but no measurement of gamma exists for a negative-mass source, since none is known. phase1 needs M < 0 (phase1.py:204).

lacked_data: What the originators had: Einstein's 1916 Newtonian limit and the Eddington-Robertson gamma, beta rested on the 1919 eclipse deflection (tens of percent) and Mercury's perihelion; the PPN framework (Nordtvedt 1968, Will 1971) on 1970s radar/VLBI at 1e-3. What came later: Cassini 2003 fixes gamma - 1 = (2.1 +- 2.3)e-5, and Messenger-era fits beta - 1 = (-4.1 +- 7.8)e-5 (Will 2014 pp.43-45, READ). Evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result: the later, far better data moved nothing -- the first-order isotropic form and gamma = beta = 1 were confirmed, and the tree's quantity (1+gamma)/gamma moves by 2e-5 (computed, C5). The exact relations d = int e^{-Phi} dl, t = int e^{-2Phi} dl are geometry of the stated metric and cannot be moved by any datum (C1). Evidence that data IS lacking, in the tree's use: every gamma measurement is for a POSITIVE-mass source; phase1 needs M < 0 (phase1.py:204). GR's linearised equations are linear in T, so GR predicts gamma = 1 for either sign, but that is a prediction; no negative-mass source exists to test it. That gap is OPEN empirically and does not change the conclusion inside GR. The one place a conclusion moves is not a datum but a regime: the tree applies the first-order law at Phi_max ~ 20 (50 % figure), where the weak-field result was never claimed to hold (Will p.28-29, W2/W3/W4).
grade_evidence: Theorem 1 as the tree states it STANDS: for the static metric g_tt = -e^{2Phi}, g_ij = e^{-2Phi} delta_ij the static observer's slice length is int e^{-Phi} dl and the coordinate light time int e^{-2Phi} dl exactly (C1, sympy), and the Newtonian identification Phi = -U with beta = gamma = 1 matches the post-Newtonian metric READ in Will 2014 Box 2 p.31 (C3); 'ratio exactly 2' is exact for the exponents and first order for the savings (1 + e^{-Phi}, C2), which the owner's own measured 1.9940-2.0229 and rtol 5e-3 already reflect; Cassini gamma moves it 2e-5 (C5); Lambda's closed form agrees with the exact full-crossing integral to 1.3e-6 (C6); G, c, M_sun move nothing (C7). NARROWED because the tree drops the weak-field hypothesis where it prices with the result: contraction_law (phase1.py:364-366) is the first-order law, and phase1.py:180-181, 508-510 and index3.py:673 apply it to 50 % of a 4 ly corridor, which requires Phi_max >= 1.85 for ANY shell geometry with the endpoints outside the shell and 19.93 at the tree's own R_s/b = 200 (C8a-b); there the exact ansatz contraction is 0.403 of the linear law (C8c), and at the 1 % figure 0.944 (C8d). Two further items are recorded, not graded against the result: the canonical name's 'Phi = G M/(c^2 r)' is the standard -GM/(c^2 r) with M the magnitude of a negative mass (phase1.py:204, 261-263); and the single-Phi ansatz is a GR vacuum only to first order (C3d, C4), which phase1 declares as its metric form. Nothing is repaired; the discrepancies are recorded.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restricting contraction_law's quoted figures to Phi_max << 1 (e.g. stating the 50 % figure as outside the law's domain), or a strong-field GR computation of the contraction at the 50 % configuration that happens to reproduce m*Lambda. To WRONG: nothing in reach -- no counterexample to the first-order relations exists; a measured gamma departing from 1 by more than ~5e-3 would move the ratio (1+gamma)/gamma outside the tree's rtol 5e-3, and Cassini's (2.1 +- 2.3)e-5 excludes that by ~200 sigma. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a measurement of gamma for a negative-mass source differing from 1 (no such source is known). To OPEN: none -- the source was read through recovered page text; if that recovery were ruled inadmissible, the source status would drop to NAMED-NOT-READ while the re-derivations (C1-C8) stand on their own.
